---
title: "Locks and Deadlocks — When Two Helpful Workers Freeze"
description: "A rigorous introductory lesson with one small example, mathematical notation and a proof-oriented explanation."
---

## Start with an ordinary situation

Two workers need locks A and B. Worker 1 holds A and waits for B; worker 2 holds B and waits for A. Nobody makes progress.

## The core concept

A lock ensures exclusion, but a poor order of lock acquisition can create a cycle of waiting.

## Express it mathematically

$$
T_1\to L_B\to T_2\to L_A\to T_1
$$

**Every symbol explained:** T_1 and T_2 are threads; L_A and L_B are locks A and B; each arrow means 'waits for a resource held by' or the corresponding resource-to-owner dependency. The cycle means no member can advance while all resources stay held.

**Substitute actual numbers:** Worker 1 owns A, requires B; worker 2 owns B, requires A. Both wait forever. If both always acquire A before B, worker 2 must wait outside before taking B, so this exact cycle cannot form.

## Why it works

The classic Coffman conditions are mutual exclusion, hold-and-wait, no preemption, and circular wait. Breaking the circular-wait condition by acquiring locks in a consistent global order can prevent this class of deadlock.

## Go one level deeper

Deadlock is distinct from a data race, starvation and livelock; safe memory access alone does not guarantee progress.

## Common misunderstanding

A deadlock detector can identify cycles in a resource graph, but it does not always imply recovery is cheap or safe.

## Check your understanding

Explain the example with different numbers. Identify which assumption makes the derivation work, and which assumption would invalidate it. Then write the mathematical model again without looking.
